opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write (role does not own Payroll, so no admin). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB for E019 (Eric Woods): contractor, basic security training. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Contractor with basic training max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Employee E019 (Eric Woods) requested write access to Payroll. Per the Security agent's note, E019 is a contractor with basic security training (both looked up in the security database). For contractors, write requires advanced security training and admin is never allowed, so the maximum permitted level is read. The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum: read.

- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security says basic → max read. Requested write exceeds max → grant read.
